A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RN-D and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. The retained material can be matched reliably despite the shortened title, renumbering, and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original PPO experiments on locomotion and manipulation tasks, including learning curves, gradient measurements, ablations, and off-policy comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds TRPO/SPO experiments and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The RN-D actor retains uniform per-dimension categorical discretization, pre-LayerNorm residual blocks, and the same output construction and critic design. TRPO and SPO provide additional optimization settings for evaluating this actor; no new RN-D architecture or parameterization component is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five Gym locomotion tasks, ten ManiSkill state tasks, and five ManiSkill RGB tasks. The added TRPO/SPO experiments reuse the state-based suites, and the runtime analysis uses existing tasks. Appendix D explicitly restricts RGB evaluation to PPO.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated TRPO- and SPO-based comparisons: Figure 1 compares their standard MLP-C implementations with RN-D, and Figures 10–11 also include RN-C and MLP-D under each algorithm. These algorithm-specific comparison suites were absent from v1. The original PPO comparator set and TD3/TD-MPC2 comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 adds TRPO natural-gradient updates with a KL constraint, conjugate gradient, backtracking, and full-batch actor updates, plus SPO's softly regularized surrogate. Appendix C.5 introduces throughput measurements alongside runtime. The existing PPO hyperparameter table and training budgets are unchanged. The new GAE paragraph does not clearly reconcile its 0.99/0.95 values with the retained ManiSkill PPO values of 0.80/0.90.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.5 examines computational sensitivity to bin count on Humanoid-v4 and compares runtime across the four actor variants. This adds a focused overhead analysis. The existing gradient/SNR analysis, loss-swap ablation, actor-width sweep, and performance-versus-bin-count study are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use five-seed reporting and 95% stratified bootstrap confidence intervals for learning curves; the three-seed TD-MPC2 disclosure also remains. New experiments extend the existing reporting practice without introducing different uncertainty estimation, significance testing, or an increased run count for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Figures 1 and 10–11 add aggregate and per-task TRPO/SPO results, showing higher aggregate performance for RN-D than MLP-C under both algorithms. New runtime tables report, for example, RN-D at 1.64 hours and 873.8 SPS versus RN-C at 1.75 hours and 811.1 SPS. Table 4 adds bin-count-dependent runtime results. Retained PPO curves and earlier ablation results are unchanged; the additions are not same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.1, its assumptions and variance bounds, and the complete Appendix A proof are unchanged. The categorical/Gaussian likelihood derivations and Appendix C.2 loss-swap equations are also retained without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit contribution that RN-D is algorithm-agnostic and benefits multiple on-policy algorithms, whereas v1 leaves evaluation beyond PPO to future work. Conversely, the abstract narrows its state-of-the-art claim to on-policy RL, and Section 7 explicitly disclaims superiority across all RL algorithms.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new algorithm comparisons as evidence that benefits are not specific to PPO's surrogate. It adds an interpretation of runtime saturation with increasing bin count and explicitly identifies TRPO memory requirements as a barrier to matching the vision-based setup. Section 7 also qualifies the preferred bin count as task-dependent.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a code-repository address. Appendix B supplies new TRPO implementation details, including KL threshold 0.01, damping 0.1, ten conjugate-gradient iterations, and backtracking settings, and reports eight RTX 6000 Pro GPUs for TRPO/SPO. Runtime tables add concrete resource measurements. These substantially extend reproducibility information, although the new cross-benchmark GAE wording remains ambiguous.

R1.justification: Section 7 reframes TD3 and TD-MPC2 as representative off-policy efficiency comparisons rather than support for unrestricted state-of-the-art positioning. The cited-work set is otherwise retained. Changes to the SPO publication year/venue and other bibliography details do not introduce new research references.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title and running header, revises the abstract, expands the introduction, and makes localized revisions to the extended-study discussion and conclusion. It adds runtime discussion, implementation paragraphs, and funding acknowledgements. The principal section organization and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a six-panel cross-algorithm overview, two substantial per-task figure grids for TRPO/SPO, and two distinct runtime tables, one repeated in the main text and appendix. Existing figures are retained and renumbered, with relocation and resizing. The new Figures 10–11 captions mention RGB variants despite Appendix D limiting those experiments to state observations.

improvement.justification: v1's broad on-policy message relied on PPO experiments. The added TRPO/SPO evidence substantially strengthens that central generality claim, while the narrowed state-of-the-art wording improves its calibration. Runtime analysis, update details, and code-access information also improve practical assessability and reproducibility. These gains outweigh limited reporting problems: the new figure captions overstate RGB coverage, and the GAE settings are not clearly reconciled across benchmarks.
